title: Streaming handshake resilience testbed and function-call jitter certification
creator: Sanjay Patel
description: Goal: Validate that newly onboarded model variants (float16, int8/quantized) behave correctly when used with streaming output and external function/tool-calling. This ticket builds a resilience testbed that injects network jitter, delayed chunk delivery, and variable tokenization boundaries to ensure handshake idempotency, KV-cache alignment, and correct function-call boundaries across model versions and pinned snapshots. Success requires deterministic function-call typing and no loss/duplication of function arguments across retries or chunk reordering. Outputs of the test will feed published performance profiles and the onboarding checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Automated test harness runs against 3 representative model families (causal, chat, instruction-following) and verifies function-call metadata is preserved across streaming chunk reorders.
Telemetry: Identify and log any off-by-one token boundaries or duplicate function-call events; no regression across pinned versions for 95% of synthetic flows.
Canary: A canary rollout that exercises handshake retry paths with a 10% synthetic jitter profile shows <0.5% error-rate on production-like traces.
Integration: Test artifacts (scripts, golden traces, assertion harness) merged to runtime repo and referenced from onboarding playbook.
steps: 1) Draft test scenarios and golden traces for function-call initiation, nested calls, and tool handshake aborts.
2) Implement a lightweight harness that proxies streaming chunks and reorders/delays them (libproxy harness under infra/tests/stream-jitter).
3) Run harness on model snapshots (v1/v2 quantized) in canary nodes and capture KV-cache deltas.
4) Add assertion logic to detect duplicated/missing function-call payloads and token boundary misalignment.
5) Publish results to onboarding Confluence page and attach artifacts to the model profile in the catalog.

notes: Trade-offs: aggressive reconnect idempotency adds per-request header overhead (approx +2KB) but avoids costly dedup reconciliation in downstream toolchains. We prefer a light-weight token rather than full session state in proxy to keep runtime stateless. Edge-case: server-side prefetch can still cause partial KV divergence — flagged for deeper runtime kernel fix if regression persists.
